description:
Create, list and show thread files. A thread is a project, process or topic that notes, logs, hours and payments attach to.

Subcommands:
  list [QUERY] [--all] [--json] — list thread files (open only by default)
  show THREAD [--json] — show one thread file
  new --name NAME --kind KIND --category CATEGORY [--currency CCY] [--rate N] — create a thread file

Args:
  QUERY: optional fuzzy search; results ranked by similarity.
  THREAD: thread name or 'Kind/Name'.

Flags:
  list:
    --all  include paused and closed threads
    --json  JSON output
  show: --json  JSON output
  new:
    --name  required. Becomes the filename; must not contain '/' or start with '.'
    --kind  required. project, process or topic; files go under Projects, Processes or Topics
    --category  required. professional, personal or voluntary
    --currency  3-letter ISO code; the default currency for `hours`. Optional
    --rate N  default hourly rate for `hours`; requires --currency

Examples:
  ["list", "northwind", "--all"]
  ["show", "Projects/Northwind", "--json"]
  ["new", "--name", "Northwind", "--kind", "project", "--category", "professional", "--currency", "ZAR", "--rate", "1500"]

Notes:
  Nothing prompts.
  Thread files live at threads/<Kind>/<Name>.md, with the thread's folder beside them.
  There is no close or delete subcommand. Closing a thread means setting status: closed and ended: in its frontmatter.
  A thread must exist before notes, hours, payments, stats or buffer entries can name it.
  Exit 1: empty name, name containing '/' or starting with '.', thread already exists, or --rate without --currency.
